title: Take-up Rate of Enhanced Shared Parental Leave
what_it_is: Take-up Rate of Enhanced Shared Parental Leave

sections.label: Shared Parental Leave take-up rate
sections.summary: The Shared Parental Leave scheme began 1 April 2025, and MSF can update the 2025 birth cohort take-up rate in mid-2027.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: The take-up rate for the new Shared Parental Leave scheme is not yet available.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: The Shared Parental Leave scheme was introduced on 1 April 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Following their Maternity or Paternity Leave, parents have up to a year after their child's birth to utilise their Shared Parental Leave.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Thereafter, their employers have an additional three months to submit their claims to the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF).

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: MSF will be able to provide an update on the Shared Parental Leave take-up rate for the 2025 birth cohort in mid-2027.

sections.label: Ten-week Shared Parental Leave
sections.summary: The 10-week Shared Parental Leave was introduced on 1 April this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: In fact, on 1 April this year, we have just introduced the 10-week Shared Parental Leave.

sections.label: Encouraging fathers' active role
sections.summary: MSF works with partners like the Centre for Fathering on programmes and outreach to encourage fathers, and says workplace norms need to change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: MSF continuously works with our partners, including partners such as the Centre for Fathering, to develop programmes and do public outreach to encourage our fathers to do more in terms of playing an active role in our children's development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: I also want to take the opportunity to say that beyond the Shared Parental Leave scheme, to encourage our fathers to do more, we do need to look beyond, perhaps at a societal reset in terms of how our workplace norms need to change, to balance more of family needs.
